instrument_name: Minimum Wage Act of 1968 (Act 5 of 1968, 43 P.S. 333.101-333.115), consolidated text
figure_or_rule_carried: Sec. 4(a)(8) 7.15/h from 2007-07-01; Sec. 4(a.1) state minimum rises automatically with FLSA (so 7.25/h since 2009-07-24, FLSA 6(a)(1)); Sec. 4(c) overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/workweek, FLSA 7(j) 8-and-80 allowed; Sec. 3(d) tip credit; Sec. 4(b) learner/student certificates not below 85%; Sec. 4(e) training wage under-20 first 60 days at FLSA 6(a) rate; Sec. 5(a) exempt from MW and OT: farm labour, domestic service in private home, newspaper delivery, EAP/outside sales, golf caddy, etc.; Sec. 5(b) OT-only exemptions (seaman, auto sales/mechanics, taxi drivers, small radio/TV announcers); Sec. 8 records kept 3 years; Sec. 14.1 preempts local minimum-wage ordinances (except those in effect 2006-01-01). Not indexed.

instrument_name: 34 Pa. Code Chapter 231 Minimum Wage (regulations), Pa. Code site current through 56 Pa.B. 5370 (2026-08-08)
authority: Pennsylvania Code & Bulletin (Department of Labor and Industry regulations)
figure_or_rule_carried: 231.101a(a) 7.25/h all hours; 231.101a(b) tipped employee cash wage 2.83/h, employer makes up shortfall; 231.1 tipped employee = customarily and regularly receives more than 135 USD/month in tips; 231.31 payroll records (13 items incl. hours daily/weekly, regular rate, additions/deductions, date of payment and period) kept 3 years from last entry; 231.34 tipped-employee records incl. tip credit notified in writing when changed; 231.43(g) regular rate of salaried non-exempt employees = remuneration / 40 hours (no fluctuating-workweek half-time); EAP salary-test sections 231.82-231.84 abrogated. 2022 amendments 52 Pa.B. 2701 effective in 90 days.

instrument_name: PA DLI Wage FAQs (minimum wage, overtime, EAP salary level, deductions, pay stub, final pay, leave)
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 7.25/h; OT 1.5x over 40 h/week, comp time in lieu of OT not legal, 8-and-80 for hospitals (Act 109 of 2012); EAP exemption salary level 684 USD/week (DLI follows the 2019 federal level, 84 FR 51307); no holiday pay, sick, vacation or severance by state law (policy/contract governs; Philadelphia city rules may add); breaks: 30 min for minors 14-17 working 5+ consecutive hours, breaks <20 min paid; deductions: written authorization per deduction, no blanket authorization at hire, cannot reduce pay below minimum wage; final pay: quit, layoff or discharge -> all monies earned by next scheduled payday; records kept 3 years.

instrument_name: PA DLI Pennsylvania's Minimum Wage Act page
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry
article_or_section: Minimum Wage Act violations; sub-minimum certificates LLC-3/LLC-4/LLC-18
figure_or_rule_carried: Second authority document for 7.25/h minimum and 2.83/h tipped cash wage; tip credit only where tips >=135/month; no deduction of card-processing fees from tips; 1.5x after 40 h; sub-minimum certificates: student LLC-3, learner LLC-4, worker with disability LLC-18.

instrument_name: Wage Payment and Collection Law (Act 329 of 1961, 43 P.S. 260.1-260.45), consolidated text
figure_or_rule_carried: Sec. 2.1 wages include fringe benefits/wage supplements (separation, vacation, holiday pay per agreement); Sec. 3(a) regular paydays designated in advance; wages due within period in written contract, or standard time lapse customary in the trade, or within 15 days after end of pay period; overtime may be paid in next succeeding period; payment in lawful money or check; deductions only as provided by law or authorized by DLI regulation; Sec. 3(b) fringe benefits/union dues remitted within 10 days of due date (60 days after claim if no date); Sec. 4 notice at hire of time/place of payment, rate, fringe benefits, and of changes before they take effect (or by posting); Sec. 5(a) separated or resigning employee: wages due not later than next regular payday, by certified mail if requested; Sec. 10 liquidated damages 25% or 500 USD, whichever greater, if unpaid >30 days after payday without good-faith dispute.

instrument_name: 34 Pa. Code 9.1 Authorized deductions (WPCL regulation)
authority: Pennsylvania Code & Bulletin (Department of Labor and Industry)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exhaustive list of permitted wage deductions under WPCL Sec. 3: ERISA plan contributions/overpayment recovery; written-authorized insurance, thrift, stock purchase, savings, bond, charity, local development deductions; deductions provided by law (Social Security, federal/local income or wage taxes, occupation privilege taxes, court orders); union dues; repayment of bona fide employer loans authorized in writing at or after the loan; purchases from employer or third parties authorized in writing; other written-authorized deductions the Department deems proper. Page current through 56 Pa.B. 5370 (2026-08-08).

instrument_name: 42 Pa.C.S. 8127 Personal earnings exempt from process
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages exempt from attachment/execution except for: divorce (23 Pa.C.S. Pt. IV); support; board for 4 weeks or less; residential-lease landlord judgments (max 10% of net wages per pay period or the amount that keeps net income at the federal poverty guideline, whichever is less; net wages = wages less federal/state/local income taxes, FICA and nonvoluntary retirement, union dues, health premiums; employer remits to prothonotary within 15 days of close of last pay period of each month, may deduct up to 5 USD bookkeeping cost; multiple lease attachments satisfied in order served); PHEAA student loans; criminal restitution/costs/fines. Priority: support first, criminal restitution second. Ordinary consumer-creditor wage garnishment is not available in PA (stricter than CCPA).

instrument_name: 23 Pa.C.S. 4392 Employer reporting (Commonwealth directory of new hires)
figure_or_rule_carried: New-hire directory within DLI; every employer doing business in PA reports: employee name, home address, SSN, date of hire; employer name, address, FEIN; employer contact name and telephone; on DLI form or by attaching hire date and contact to the W-4; mail, magnetic or electronic; multistate employers transmitting electronically may designate one state (notify PA directory and HHS); deadline 20 days from date of hire, or two monthly electronic transmissions 12-16 days apart.

instrument_name: PA DOR Employer Withholding page (local copy 2026-11-02, re-read of US-PA-002)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold PA PIT from residents (services in or outside PA) and nonresidents (services in PA) at flat 3.07%; deposit schedule quarterly <300/qtr (last day of Apr, Jul, Oct, Jan), monthly 300-999/qtr (15th of following month), semi-monthly 1,000-4,999.99/qtr (3 banking days after close of semi-monthly period), semi-weekly >=5,000/qtr or 20,000/yr (Wednesday after Wed-Fri paydays; Friday after Sat-Tue paydays); Quarterly Withholding Return W-3 plus W-2s and transmittal; due-date card REV-1716; W-2 employees under Employer Withholding account, 1099 withholding under a separate Other Income Withholding account; 10 or more income statements must be filed electronically (myPATH).

instrument_name: PA DOR W-2 Electronic Filing Requirement and myPATH Employer Withholding File Upload Specs index
article_or_section: W-2 Electronic Filing Requirement; File Upload Specs list
figure_or_rule_carried: REV-1667 Annual Withholding Reconciliation Statement filed in myPATH by January 31 with W-2s filed electronically; myPATH upload formats listed: Employer PA-501 (deposit), PA W-2 Wage Records (EFW2) and (CSV), corrected PA-W2 (EFW2C) and (CSV), 1099-R/MISC/NEC records, REV-1667 transmittal. Field-level specs are on the sub-pages (not fetched in Stage 5: RSPEC scope).

instrument_name: PA Personal Income Tax Guide - Gross Compensation chapter
article_or_section: Income items always/never taxable as PA compensation; Pennsylvania Taxation of Cafeteria Plans; retirement plans
figure_or_rule_carried: Departures from federal: employee contributions/elective deferrals to 401(k), 403(b), 457(b) and any retirement plan are taxable PA compensation when made (employer contributions not taxed at contribution); Section 125: employee salary reductions for health/accident/hospitalization/disability/life coverage excluded to the extent federally excluded, but salary reductions for dependent care and 401 plans are NOT excludable; employer cash reimbursement of dependent care is taxable (example 50/month -> 600 on W-2), employer-provided dependent care facility is not; employer-paid group-term life premiums never taxable (no 50,000 imputed-income rule); personal use of employer property (incl. company car), employer-provided parking, meals and lodging are nontaxable fringes; severance, covenant-not-to-compete, sick pay representing regular wages taxable; household employee pay taxable; nonqualified (409A) deferrals not taxable when deferred, distributions taxed. Detail form REV-634 not fetched.

instrument_name: PA Personal Income Tax Guide - Deductions and Credits chapter
article_or_section: Deductions; Resident Credit for Tax Paid to Another State
figure_or_rule_carried: Only four PA deductions: Archer MSA, HSA, 529 and 529A contributions; PA follows federal rules and limits for MSA/HSA contributions (deduction on PA Schedule O). Resident credit for tax paid to another state on the same income (from 2014 a foreign country is not a state for the credit). Whether payroll may exclude HSA salary reductions from PA withholding is not stated on this page (open question).

instrument_name: PA DLI UC-2INS Instructions for Completing PA UC Quarterly Tax Forms (UC-2, UC-2A), REV 09-23
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, Office of UC Tax Services
article_or_section: Due dates; Internet filing; Items 1-11 (UC-2) and 1-9 (UC-2A); taxable wage base table
figure_or_rule_carried: UC-2 (employer report: gross wages, employee contributions = gross x employee rate, taxable wages, contributions) and UC-2A (per employee: SSN, name, gross wages paid in quarter, credit weeks) due April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31 (next business day if weekend/holiday); zero report required if no wages (UC-2A not required then); all employers must file online (UCMS, www.uctax.pa.gov), temporary waiver possible; electronic payment mandatory once liability >= 5,000 for a payment period (penalty 10% of payment for non-compliance, capped); wages reported in quarter paid, not earned; credit week = calendar week with remuneration >= 116 USD (incl. holiday and vacation pay); late-report penalty 15% of contributions, min 125, max 450; employer taxable wage base 10,000 (2018 and thereafter).

instrument_name: PA DLI Form UC-1609 Employer Information for Separating Employees (REV 08-24), under UC Law Sec. 206.1
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, Office of UC Benefits
article_or_section: UC Law Sec. 206.1 (43 P.S. 766.1, added by Act 9 of 2020)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer must notify separating employees, at the time of separation, of the availability of UC benefits (UC Law Sec. 206.1); UC-1609 recommended but another format allowed; employer portion: PA UC account number or FEIN, address for UC-45 Notice of Application, contact person/email, estimated return-to-work date if recall (MM/DD/YY). Spanish edition UC-1609(ESP) published. Act 9 of 2020 also covers reduction of hours (per search lead; the form page itself names separation).

instrument_name: City of Philadelphia, Office of the Managing Director Regulations regarding Phila. Code Chapter 9-4100 Promoting Healthy Families and Workplaces (paid sick leave), memo dated 2016-04-13
authority: City of Philadelphia, Office of the Managing Director (filed with Department of Records)
figure_or_rule_carried: Paid sick time required where the employer employs 10 or more employees for at least 40 weeks in a calendar year (smaller employers: unpaid sick time); an Employee must work within Philadelphia at least 40 hours a year; accrued unused sick time carries over but an employee may not accrue or use more than 40 hours in a calendar year; front-loading 40 hours at start of year removes the carry-over duty; PTO policy complies if it gives at least 40 hours usable under all 9-4100 conditions; rehire within 6 months restores prior unused accrued time. The accrual rate itself (lead: 1 hour per 40 hours worked, tier B) is in Code 9-4104, not read: ordinance text on amlegal 403.

instrument_name: City of Pittsburgh press bulletin: updates to the Paid Sick Days Act (ceremonial signing), 2025-07-07
authority: City of Pittsburgh, Mayor's Office / Office of Equal Protection
article_or_section: Paid Sick Days Act (Pittsburgh Code ch. 626) amendment
figure_or_rule_carried: City Council unanimously approved (June 2025) amendments increasing the accrual rate and the maximum accumulation of paid sick leave starting in 2026 (quote refers to '40 hours a year - or even 72 hours per year'); employers must maintain a PSD policy, give notice of rights, and submit policy and notice to paidsickleave@pittsburghpa.gov. Exact 2026 numbers (lead, tier B: 1 hour per 30 hours worked; cap 72 h for 15+ employees, 48 h for <15) NOT confirmed on an authority page: pittsburghpa.gov returned 403 (direct and Wayback).

instrument_name: Local Tax Enabling Act (Act 511 of 1965, 53 P.S. 6924.101 ff.), consolidated text incl. Act 32 of 2008 Chapter 5
figure_or_rule_carried: EIT (Sec. 512): employer with a place of business in a tax collection district (excluding domestic servants) deducts at payment the GREATER of the employee's resident EIT or nonresident EIT per the DCED official register; temporary assignments: <90 consecutive days at a job location -> based on employer's permanent home office, >=90 days -> job location; Philadelphia workers excluded where subject to the Sterling Act; new employees (and on address change) complete a certificate of residency as addendum to W-4; quarterly return and payment by the last day of the month following each quarter to the tax officer for each employee's place of employment (name, address, SSN, compensation, tax, political subdivisions); multi-district employers may elect combined monthly electronic filing with one tax officer (notice 1 month ahead); repeat failures -> monthly filing; annual return and individual withholding statement (may be integrated with W-2) by February 28 with the PSD work-location code (format xxxxxx-xx where single-collector election). LST (Sec. 301.1): maximum 52 USD per person per calendar year irrespective of number of jurisdictions; levies >10 USD collected pro rata per payroll period (annual rate / employer's number of payroll periods, rounded DOWN to the cent); levies >10 USD must exempt persons with earned income + net profits in the subdivision < 12,000 USD (optional for <=10 USD levies); mandatory exemptions for 100% disabled veterans and reservists called to active duty; situs = place of employment on first day of each payroll period (>10 USD) or of the year (<=10 USD); one subdivision per payroll period with priority principal office -> residence-and-work -> nearest to home; concurrent employment: non-principal employer refrains on a recent principal-employer pay statement plus employee statement. Sec. 312: LST remitted 30 days after end of each quarter.

instrument_name: PA DCED Local Income Tax Requirements for Employers (local copy 2026-11-02, re-read of US-PA-004)
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Community & Economic Development
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with worksites in PA withhold and remit EIT and LST for employees working in PA; worksites include factories, warehouses, branches, offices and RESIDENCES OF HOME-BASED EMPLOYEES; step 1 look up PSD codes, EIT and LST rates in the DCED Address Search Application; step 2 Residency Certification Form per employee kept in personnel file; step 3 register with the local tax collector(s) for a local tax ID; step 4 withhold and remit, quarterly filings and remittances within 30 days after quarter end (collector website or paper Employer's Quarterly EIT Return); W2-R Annual Reconciliation by the last day of February. Rates are per address (no single table): rate lookup is a DCED application, not a static file.

instrument_name: Unemployment Compensation Law (Act of Dec. 5, 1936, 2nd Sp. Sess., P.L. 2897, No. 1, 43 P.S. 751 ff.), consolidated text incl. Act 55 of 2025
figure_or_rule_carried: Sec. 4(x)(1): employer-contribution wage base 10,000 per employee per calendar year for 2018 and thereafter (statutory, not indexed; predecessor wages creditable); Sec. 301.4: employee contributions on ALL wages without the 4(x)(1) limit at the rate set under Sec. 301.7, employer withholds in trust at payment and remits; Sec. 4(l)(4) exclusions from 'employment': agricultural labour except farms covered under 4(l)(3)(G); domestic service in a private home/college club/fraternity EXCEPT covered where cash remuneration >= 1,000 USD in any calendar quarter of current or preceding year; casual non-trade service < 50 USD/quarter; service for son, daughter or spouse and by a child under 18 for a parent; federal service; for Arts. X-XII churches/religious organizations and ministers in their ministry; students employed by their school and spouses under financial-aid programs; student nurses; newspaper delivery under 18; full-time students in certain camps. Act 55 of 2025 (2025-12-22, P.L.333): Sec. 402.7 domestic-violence eligibility with automatic relief from benefit charges for base-year employers.

instrument_name: Privacy of Social Security Numbers Law (Act 60 of 2006, 74 P.S. 201)
figure_or_rule_carried: No person or entity may: publicly post/display an SSN; print an SSN on a card required to access products or services; require SSN transmission over the Internet unless the connection is secure or encrypted; require SSN alone to access a website; print an SSN on materials mailed to the individual unless federal or state law requires it (if mailed, never visible on postcard/envelope). No pay-statement SSN-truncation rule in the act (no requirement to show or truncate SSN on pay stubs; a mailed paper pay stub must not carry the SSN since no law requires it there). Effective date per act: 180 days after enactment (computed 2006-12-26; not separately verified).

instrument_name: Breach of Personal Information Notification Act (Act 94 of 2005, 73 P.S. 2301 ff.), as amended by Act 151 of 2022 and Act 33 of 2024
figure_or_rule_carried: Entities maintaining computerized personal information (incl. SSN) of PA residents notify affected residents without unreasonable delay after discovery; where more than 500 PA individuals are notified, concurrent notice to the Office of Attorney General (org name/location, breach date, summary, totals) and notice to nationwide consumer reporting agencies (Act 33 of 2024); where SSN, bank account or driver's licence/state ID number is involved, offer one independent credit report and 12 months of credit monitoring at no cost (Act 33 of 2024). Effective date of Act 33 amendments computed as 90 days after 2024-06-28 (not separately verified).

instrument_name: City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue - Wage Tax (employers) page, local copy 2026-11-02
authority: City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue
article_or_section: Tax rate; Who pays; Quarterly filing schedule; Payment frequency; rate history
figure_or_rule_carried: Rates: from 2026-07-01 resident 3.735%, non-resident 3.425%; 2025-07-01 3.74%/3.43%; 2024-07-01 and 2023-07-01 3.75%/3.44%; 2022-07-01 3.79%/3.44%; rates scheduled to keep falling over five years from TY2025 (no future rate published). Residents taxed wherever they work; non-residents on work performed in Philadelphia; every PA-located employer of a Philadelphia resident or of a non-resident working in Philadelphia registers with the City within 30 days and withholds. Quarterly returns on the Philadelphia Tax Center (2026: Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Feb 1 2027); no paper returns; annual reconciliation no longer required (Q4 is final); payment frequency by amount withheld: <350/month quarterly, 350-16,000/month monthly, >=16,000/month semi-monthly (bi-monthly payrolls) or weekly; W-2s also submitted to the City; income-based 1.5% rate via refund for PA tax-forgiveness filers. Corroborates and adds the local file to US-PAP7-006 (same figures).
